title: Instagram Reels Trends This Week (November 2026, Updated Weekly)

body_markdown:
**A Reels trend lives two or three weeks now. This page is the short version: the formats working on Instagram right now, checked against several trend trackers, sorted by the kind of business they fit, with the comment keyword that turns the views into DMs.**

## Three questions: fit, sound, ask


Most businesses jump on trends the same way: see a funny Reel, copy it, get some views, wonder why nobody booked. The format was fine. The choice was random. Run every trend through three questions first.

## Reels trends this week: November 17–23, 2026


Trend 01


Spotted · November 20, 2026


### I feel like I haven't done much this year


Example:[@finding.jules](https://www.instagram.com/reel/DfnKK0av0w-/) · 480K views


**What it is.** The year-end recap with a twist. The Reel opens on the line "I feel like I haven't done much this year…", then flips through one short clip per month, each labeled with the month's name. By December the viewer has watched you do a lot.


**How to shoot it.**


1. Pick one clip or photo per month from your camera roll. Twelve moments, about one second each.
2. Put the opening line on screen over the first clip.
3. Label each clip with the month. Cut on the beat. Total length: 12–20 seconds.


♫


[Coming Up Roses — Harry Styles](https://www.instagram.com/reels/audio/1969670177763370/) . Licensed track: check it on a business account.


Trend 02


Spotted · November 20, 2026


### Dear Santa, I'm a size…


Example:[@blobyblouk](https://www.instagram.com/reel/DfSiCRHofa5/) · 45K views


**What it is.** A text joke with a sales punchline. The on-screen text starts "Dear Santa, I'm a size…" and ends with a wish that doesn't come in sizes: a facial, a trip, a full set of lashes, the product you sell.


**How to shoot it.**


1. One shot, 5–10 seconds. You, the product or the treatment room.
2. Text line one: "Dear Santa, I'm a size…"
3. Text line two: the wish. "…a size 'lip filler before New Year'."


♫


[Last Christmas (Instrumental) — Wham!](https://www.instagram.com/reels/audio/798069364260186/) . The instrumental version is easier to find on business accounts.


Trend 03


Spotted · November 13, still trending the week of November 17


### Appointment timestamps


Example:[@gels.by.maria](https://www.instagram.com/reel/DbQcmnVNJMh/) · 6.7K views


**What it is.** One appointment from walking in to walking out, with a timestamp on every clip: 10:02 arrival, 10:05 consultation, 10:40 the reveal. It answers the question every new client is afraid to ask: what actually happens, and how long does it take?


**How to shoot it.**


1. Ask a regular client if you can film their visit. Film short clips at each step.
2. Add the real time to each clip as on-screen text.
3. End on the result and the walk-out. 15–30 seconds.


♫


[original audio](https://www.instagram.com/reels/audio/27734209222913191/) . Original audio is usually available to business accounts.


Trend 04


Spotted · weeks of November 10 and 17, 2026


### The switch to Christmas


Example:[@cowgirlgoldfish](https://www.tiktok.com/@cowgirlgoldfish/video/7703331996851784973) · 2.7M views


**What it is.** A before-and-after from the same camera spot: November "before", cut on the beat, full Christmas "after". Mariah Carey's song is back at number one on TikTok this month, and "It's time!" decor reveals are everywhere.


**How to shoot it.**


1. Fix the phone on a tripod. Film the space as it is now.
2. Decorate. Film the same frame from the same spot.
3. Cut on the beat drop and add one line: what's open, bookable or new for December.


♫


[All I Want for Christmas Is You — Mariah Carey](https://www.instagram.com/reels/audio/241218059790539/) . Licensed track. Michael Bublé's "It's Beginning to Look a Lot like Christmas" is the other big sound for this format.


Trend 05


Spotted · week of November 17, 2026


### The slow festive walk-through


Example:[@fredbakery](https://www.instagram.com/reel/DfkZwmpxFPd/) · 18K views


**What it is.** No jokes, no text. A slow, steady pan through a decorated space, close-ups of the details, and the full view at the end. It looks calm in a feed full of fast cuts, which is the point.


**How to shoot it.**


1. Walk slowly with the phone at chest height, or use a gimbal.
2. Stop on three or four details: the product on the shelf, the coffee bar, the view from the window.
3. End on the widest frame. 15–25 seconds.


♫


[Christmas Market — Eoneun](https://www.instagram.com/reels/audio/862197499691767/) . An instrumental, one of the safer picks for business accounts.


Trend 06


Spotted · week of November 17, at its peak


### Then and now


Example:[@saban.the.shepard](https://www.tiktok.com/@saban.the.shepard/video/7706575714291666207) · 5.6M views


**What it is.** An old photo, then the same pose, place or skill today. The cut lands on a strong beat, and the years go on screen. It's one of the most-used sounds on both Reels and TikTok this month, close to half a million videos on each.


**How to shoot it.**


1. Find a photo from your first year in business: the first chair, the first office, the first client.
2. Recreate it: same angle, same pose.
3. Cut from old to new on the beat. Add the years: "2019 → 2026".


♫


[Time — Pink Floyd](https://www.instagram.com/reels/audio/486665065097971/) . Licensed track: check it on a business account.


Trend 07


Spotted · week of November 23, ahead of Black Friday on November 27


### The Black Friday story reveal


Example:[@indigo.ca](https://www.tiktok.com/@indigo.ca/video/7710295695953251602) · 425K views


**What it is.** A 10–15 second mini-movie that doesn't look like an ad until the last second. Keep the brand out of the frame, build tension with a beat-drop track, reveal the offer and the date on the final beat.


**How to shoot it.**


1. Film a small story: a box being carried, a door being unlocked, a hand reaching for a shelf.
2. Don't show the logo or the product until the end.
3. Last frame: the discount, the date and the keyword.


♫


No single sound owns this trend. Use any dramatic beat-drop track available to your account.


Trend 08


Spotted · November 6, rising again this week


### The Blue Danube chore ballet


Example:[@austinjamespilates](https://www.instagram.com/reel/Dfj5jPvzqgB/) · 13K views


**What it is.** Treat an ordinary task like a grand ballet: a tailor slicing an apple, a Pilates instructor cleaning the studio, a groomer drying a dog, all set to the waltz. It's absurd, and it shows the work people never see.


**How to shoot it.**


1. Pick a routine task that's part of your service: cleaning, prepping, packing an order.
2. Film it with exaggerated, graceful movements. Slow motion helps.
3. Keep it to 10–20 seconds.


♫


[The Blue Danube Waltz — Royal Symphony Orchestra](https://www.instagram.com/reels/audio/2488033034771649/) . A classical recording, one of the safer picks for business accounts.

## Earlier in November 2026


Trends from previous weeks. Some are still alive; check the sound's page in the app before you film.


### Why would I deceive you?


Spotted · November 13, 2026


Example:[@jahzuuuu](https://www.tiktok.com/@jahzuuuu/video/7683983473098460446) · 931K views


An ironic line from a documentary trailer, used over an offer that sounds too good to be true. Use it only when the offer is real: "50% off your first visit. Why would I deceive you?"


### You're under arrest


Spotted · November 17, 2026


Example:[@illit_official](https://www.tiktok.com/@illit_official/video/7697995852677139732) · 16.4M views


A relay challenge: one person "arrests" the next, who passes it on. An easy way to introduce the whole team in one Reel.


### You paid me no mind


Spotted · November 17, 2026


Example:[@averykroll1](https://www.tiktok.com/@averykroll1/video/7704528703677615373) · 7.2M views


A dramatic meme audio over tiny letdowns: the coffee you forgot, the message nobody answered. Cafés and service businesses flip it into a customer joke: "When you message a salon and they reply on Tuesday."


### Toggle on


Spotted · October 30, 2026


Example:[@katiengoshair](https://www.instagram.com/reel/De1zHpsRXMa/) · 68K views


An animated ON switch as a news-alert hook: holiday hours on, new service on, booking on. Short and easy to make in any editor.


♫


[original audio](https://www.instagram.com/reels/audio/29285135541104810/)


## How to turn trend views into DMs


A trending Reel can bring ten times your usual reach in a day. Then the comments arrive at 11 p.m. on a Saturday, and by Monday the people who asked "price?" have forgotten your name. Answer the comment where it happens:


1. Pick one keyword per Reel and put it in the caption and the last frame: "Comment BOOK."
2. Set up a comment autoreply for that keyword. It posts a short public reply under the comment ("Sent you the details!") and a private DM with the link, the price or the free slots.
3. When the person replies in DMs, the AI agent keeps the conversation going: answers questions, collects their contact, books the appointment.


(1) the reel


Want the 10:02 slot? Comment **BOOK**


BOOK


(2) the autoreply


@maria.r BOOK


Sent you the free slots in DMs!


(3) the DM


Hi Maria! Tomorrow: 10:00, 12:30 or 16:00. Which one works?


12:30 please


Booked. See you tomorrow!


In Chatfuel this is a custom automation with a keyword rule in **Fuely AI → Automations → Instagram → post & reel comments** . You can point it at one Reel or all of them. The full setup is in our guide to[Instagram auto-reply to comments](https://chatfuel.com/blog/instagram-auto-reply-comments) , and[Instagram Reels for business](https://chatfuel.com/blog/instagram-reels-for-marketing) covers the rest of the Reels basics.


## The one rule


Trends are a vehicle, not a destination. The point isn't to post every trend; it's to put your offer in front of new people in a format they already enjoy, and to catch them while they're interested.


The one rule


One trend a week. One keyword.


Reply ready before you post.


## FAQ


### What is trending on Instagram Reels right now?


This week (November 17–23, 2026) the strongest formats for businesses are the year recap "I feel like I haven't done much this year", the "Dear Santa, I'm a size…" text joke, appointment timestamps and the switch to Christmas. Then and now with Pink Floyd's "Time" is at its peak on both Reels and TikTok.


### What are the trending Instagram Reels audios this week?


Coming Up Roses (Harry Styles), All I Want for Christmas Is You (Mariah Carey), Time (Pink Floyd), Christmas Market (Eoneun) and The Blue Danube Waltz. Licensed songs may be unavailable on business accounts; check in the app before you film.


### How often is this page updated?


Every week. The newest trends go to the top, and older ones move to the archive. Each trend shows the date it was spotted.


### How do you pick the trends?


We follow several trend trackers in English, Spanish and Portuguese, TikTok Creative Center and Instagram's trending-audio signals, and only list formats reported in the last two weeks. We skip trends that only work for personal creator accounts.


### Can business accounts use trending audio on Instagram?


Not always. Licensed songs are often unavailable to business accounts. Original-audio versions and instrumentals usually work. For paid ads, use Meta's royalty-free sound collection.


### How do I find trending audio in the Instagram app?


In the Reels editor, open the audio library: trending sounds are marked with an upward arrow. On any Reel, tap the audio name to see how many Reels use it.


### How do I get leads from a trending Reel?


Ask viewers to comment a keyword and reply to each comment with a DM automatically. Chatfuel's comment autoreply sends a public reply and a private message with your link or booking options, and the AI agent continues the conversation from there.
